reasoning: FCF yield 4.3% -- below my 5% floor. EV/EBIT 44.9x -- no deep value here at any angle. Market cap $105B on $4.5B FCF is 22.6x EV/FCF. SBC ~$1.8B annually eats 40% of reported FCF; real shareholder FCF yield is closer to 2.7%. Debt-to-equity clean at 0.19, net cash $2.8B -- balance sheet fine. Insider net buying +498k shares last 6m is the lone bull signal. AI dual thesis: Now Assist is real incremental revenue, not a moat -- every hyperscaler sells workflow AI now. The disruption risk is genuine and underpriced: agentic AI (Copilot, Salesforce Agentforce, startups) attacks ITSM ticketing directly, the core monetization engine. At $102 the stock prices in 22%+ perpetual revenue growth. Any deceleration -- AI substitution, enterprise budget shift -- and FCF multiples compress hard. Bear case: 20% FCF miss + 25x multiple = $88/share. Valuation leaves no margin of safety. Pass.

ai_disruption_assessment.opportunity: Now Assist (GenAI embedded in platform) adds AI SKU upsell to existing enterprise contracts. 22% revenue growth suggests AI monetization is real and landing. High switching costs (workflow automation deeply embedded) give time to adapt.
ai_disruption_assessment.threat: Agentic AI (Microsoft Copilot, Salesforce Agentforce, vertical-specific AI agents) attacks ITSM ticket routing and resolution directly -- the billable event that drives ServiceNow's per-seat/consumption model. Commoditization of ITSM logic is the structural bear case. If AI resolves tickets autonomously, enterprises question why they pay $X per seat for the workflow layer.
ai_disruption_assessment.burry_verdict: AI threat is real and the valuation prices in zero disruption probability. That asymmetry is dangerous at 44.9x EV/EBIT. Not a short -- balance sheet and FCF generation are real -- but no margin of safety for a long.
